name: Kasa KP115

matter.note: TP-Link lists Alexa, Google Assistant and SmartThings for the KP115 and doesn't mention Matter, but never says it has none. TP-Link's Matter version of this plug is the KP125M.

apple_home.note: TP-Link's KP115 platform list names Alexa, Google Assistant and SmartThings, not HomeKit, but doesn't rule it out. Kasa's HomeKit plugs are the KP125 and EP25.

google_home.note: Cloud-to-cloud link between the Kasa and Google accounts.

alexa.note: Cloud-to-cloud link via the Kasa skill.

smartthings.note: TP-Link lists Samsung SmartThings among the KP115's platforms.

home_assistant.note: Listed by the official TP-Link Smart Home integration, which talks to Kasa plugs locally.

hubRequired.note: Connects straight to 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi; TP-Link says no hub is required.

localControl.note: Home Assistant's integration controls Kasa plugs over the local network. The Kasa app itself goes through the cloud.

energyMonitoring.note: Real-time and historical power use in the Kasa app.

summary: The Kasa KP115 is a slim US Wi-Fi plug with energy monitoring, rated 15 A / 1800 W. It works with Alexa, Google Home and SmartThings through your Kasa account, and Home Assistant's official TP-Link integration controls it locally. TP-Link doesn't list Apple Home or Matter for it; its HomeKit and Matter versions are the KP125 and KP125M.
caveats: TP-Link doesn't list Apple Home or Matter; look at the KP125 (HomeKit) or KP125M (Matter) instead.
Energy data is in the Kasa app; Home Assistant users report the daily total needs the plug to reach an NTP server.
